ImageDescription.value: A view of the Brua village in the northern Indian state of Himachal Pradesh, showing a typical Kinnauri village with terraced apple, walnut and apricot orchards and narrow lanes and stairways. The buildings at the lower end of the village (bottom left corner) are situated at an altitude of about 1,990 m (6,530 feet) while the higher part of the village (top right corner) is at a height of about 2,500 m (8,200 feet). The village had remained inaccessible via road until recently. This photo has been taken from the Karchham-Sangla connecting highway located across the Baspa river, which flows below the village at about 1,960 m (6,430 feet) height.

ImageDescription.value: The hand-cut flower glass vase of Liao excavate in the upper story of the pagoda of Dule Temple was made of soda-lime glass, similar to Islamic glass.
